messages:
incident-bot: Paging: high spike in 401/429 from multiple client IPs behind a small set of proxies. Seen across edge clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Autoscale healthy but token churn causing proxy fanout. Investigating. @ryan (oncall) please triage.
ryan (oncall): Ack. Looking at auth logs now. Initial metric: auth_fail_rate 12x baseline, avg reqs/s from top ASN ~ 20k. Any IP block history?
sara (prod-eng): We're seeing repeated token refresh failures retries -> amplify. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/embeddings/batch. Some customers reporting latency/errors.
alice (sre): Can we confirm if this is a credential stuffing attempt vs misconfigured crawler? Any user-agent patterns?
mike (netsec): Early signal: user-agent mostly empty or generic curl/python, and X-Forwarded-For looks rotated through a cloud-proxy set. ASN 39520 shows heavy volume. Feels like credential spray via proxy farm. Recommend WAF block + rate-slice on edge for that ASN.
ryan (oncall): Agreed. Immediate mitigations: 1) temp WAF rule to block ASN 39520 on auth endpoints 2) apply per-ip token bucket 10r/s for /v1/embeddings/batch 3) disable batch endpoints for anonymous keys as safety net. I'll run 1 and 2 now.
alice (sre): Noted. If we disable batch endpoints, need announcement to support/AE so they don't escalate. Ben, can you prepare a short message?
ben (support): On it. Draft ready: "We're temporarily limiting batch embeddings for unverified keys due to abusive traffic. If you see errors, reach out to support." Will post once we commit action.
ryan (oncall): Applying WAF rule:
```
# wafctl add-rule --name block-asn-39520 --match "asn=39520 AND path =~ \"^/v1/(auth|embeddings|chat)\"" --action block --ttl 1800
```
alice (sre): I see the rule hitting in edge logs. Matching IPs start dropping. Auth failures dropping to 4x baseline. Good.
mike (netsec): Also pushing a quick rate-slice via edge config to shape traffic: 10r/s per src_ip, 100r/s per /24, enforced on /v1/embeddings/batch and /v1/chat/stream.
ryan (oncall): Implemented. Telemetry shows token churn reduced and proxy fanout dampened. Latency for normal traffic back to SLO. Still some residual 401s for a handful of legitimate customers — likely over-aggressive.
sara (prod-eng): Noted. Which customers impacted? Ben, can you collate the support tickets and affected API keys so we can whitelist verified keys?
ben (support): Collating now. I see 6 customers with errors in last 15m. Two are enterprise trial accounts — I'm pinging their CSMs.
alice (sre): Action item: whitelist the 6 verified API keys and add a temporary exemption:
```
edgectl set-rate-limit --scope api_key:<key> --limit 200r/s --window 60
```
ryan (oncall): Done for 4 keys (low friction). Two keys require verification from billing — Ben to follow up.
mike (netsec): Also logging note: crawler is rotating through ~1k exit proxies, so ASN block reduces pressure but consider adding a header challenge (CAPTCHA/JS) for unknown UA on auth endpoints if we see recurrence.
sara (prod-eng): Agree. Medium-term: add challenge and stricter ephemeral token throttles for refresh flows. Create an RFC?
alice (sre): Created RFC-1357 tracking: "auth hardening & probe challenge". Links and owners in product board.
ben (support): Support message posted to affected customers and Slack #customer-notices. CSMs looped. Customers acknowledged. :thumbsup:
ryan (oncall): Monitoring: keep WAF rule for now, will reduce TTL to 600s in 30m if stable. Handoff to alice for 1h follow-up and to sara for product-side mitigations. Oncall next shift at 2105556840 — @alice please escalate if needed.
alice (sre): Taking handoff. I'll keep rule live and start a rolling relaxation plan. If auth failures creep above 2x baseline, I'll reapply stricter block.
sara (prod-eng): I'll own the postmortem and mitigation RFC. Will include customer impact log, timeline, and proposed challenge flow.
incident-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0021 (abuse-proxy-fanout). Severity: P2. Participants: ryan (oncall), alice (sre), mike (netsec), sara (prod-eng), ben (support).
ryan (oncall): One more: saved extraction of edge logs filtered for ASN 39520 and paths saved to /tmp/abuse-2105556789.log for the postmortem.
alice (sre): I'll take the next 30m then hand to oncall-2. If anything spikes, page oncall. Otherwise closing active mitigation at 2105556845 and converting to monitoring mode.
